t:
No part of any appropriation contained in this Act may be obligated for the construction of quarters, including heating and plumbing apparatus, wiring and fixtures, in continental United States, except in Alaska, for greater amounts per unit than follow:

Permanent construction:


For commissioned officer, $10,000.


For commissioned warrant or warrant officer, $7,500.


For enlisted man, $6,000.




Temporary construction:


For commissioned officer, $7,500.


For commissioned warrant or warrant officer, $5,000.


For enlisted man, $3,500.

fable.w: This section only sets per-unit cost ceilings on the use of appropriated funds for building military quarters. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act may be obligated for the construction of quarters

qwen_block.w: This section establishes specific funding caps for the construction of military quarters. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or decision-making process with parties outside the federal government. The text is purely a fiscal limitation on federal spending.
qwen_block.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act may be obligated for the construction of quarters... for greater amounts per unit than follow:

opus.w: This section only sets the most that can be spent per unit when building military quarters with appropriated funds. It does not involve consulting or coordinating with anyone outside the federal government, and it creates no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue. Like Example 1, it is just a funding rule, so it does not count as participation.

opus.b:
**Step 1: Reasoning.** A reader might look for some process in this spending limit, but there isn't one. The section only caps how much appropriated money can be spent per unit on military quarters. Nobody outside the federal government is consulted, and there's no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue.

**Step 2: Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section establishes maximum cost limits for the construction of military quarters. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation by parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities) in the decision-making process. The text only restricts federal spending amounts.
qwen_chat.s: No part of any appropriation contained in this Act may be obligated for the construction of quarters... for greater amounts per unit than follow:
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that setting cost limits for construction implies a process where contractors or local entities participate in bidding or planning. However, the text itself only sets statutory caps on spending; it does not describe any consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory role for outside parties. The actors mentioned (commissioned officers, warrant officers, enlisted men) are federal employees, and the decision-making authority rests entirely with the federal government regarding how to spend the appropriated funds within those limits.
